messages:
maria (oncall): FYI we just got a priority ticket — customer on hosted inference seeing large spike of 504s on /v1/generate starting ~10:40 UTC. Error rate ~28% during a short burst. Root thread here so we can coordinate.
lee (support): Customer reports: 'requests hang for ~60s then 504. We see some 502s earlier.' Attached request ids: rid=abc123, abc124, abc129. They said this only during a burst from their end (burst traffic test).
jonathan (sre): Looking at ingress logs now — gateway returning 504: upstream connect timeout, and a slew of 502s: connection reset by peer. Appears backend pods weren't ready when traffic hit.
rahul (infra): I pulled KEDA metrics for the namespace. ScaledObject for model-pool has minReplicaCount=0, cooldownPeriod=300s, pollingInterval=30s. During the spike we had to cold-start GPUs + model init ~80–120s. KEDA didn't scale fast enough.
emily (ml-op): Model init logs from pod model-abc-0 show heavy startup: loading quantized weights and running warmup compilation, took 1m45s before becoming ready. Readiness probe timeout is 30s so kube removed pod from endpoints until it passed probe.
lee (support): Customer also saw some 403s early on — maybe token mismatch? They said some requests returned 403 then subsequent 504s.
billing-bot: ACCOUNT ALERT: Customer account flagged for payment failure 2026-11-01. Access status: active but rate-limited to 10req/s until billing clears. (This is simulated test event for thread.)
anika (customer-success): @lee — can you confirm whether billing-bot action would change token validity? Customer insists nothing changed on their side.
jonathan (sre): Billing rate-limits shouldn't yield 403s normally, would return 429. 403 suggests auth layer rejecting token. I see in proxy logs: 403 for token=tok_XYZ with message 'token revoked'. Need to check auth-service events.
rahul (infra): Quick checks:
```
kubectl get hpa -n hosted-models
kubectl get scaledobject -n hosted-models model-pool
kubectl logs -l app=model-loader -c init -n hosted-models --since=15m
```
I ran them — HPA backoff was fine, but KEDA polling interval means we only noticed queue length spike ~30s after traffic started.
emily (ml-op): So chain is: billing flagged (maybe unrelated) -> some tokens revoked for testing? -> auth rejects some tokens -> some clients retry -> gateway overloads -> KEDA starts scale -> pods start but fail readiness due to short probe time -> steady 5xx/504s.
maria (oncall): For immediate mitigation, propose:
- Temporarily route this customer's traffic to a fallback model variant with warm instances (dedicated burst pool) via routing rule.
- Set minReplicaCount=1 for the scaledobject for this customer workload to avoid cold starts while we investigate.
- Increase readiness probe timeout to 180s for model containers that do heavy init.
- Disable billing temporary rate-limit for the account so we can reproduce cleanly.
rahul (infra): I can set minReplicaCount=1 and bump readiness/liveness timeout. Making change now.

rahul (infra): (applied)
```
# patch scaledobject
kubectl patch scaledobject model-pool -n hosted-models --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/scaleTargetRef/minReplicaCount","value":1}]'
# patch deployment probe
kubectl patch deployment model-loader -n hosted-models --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"model-loader","readinessProbe":{"timeoutSeconds":180}}]}}}}'
```
jonathan (sre): After ramping minReplica and probe timeout we see backend endpoints healthy and 200s in logs. Error rate falling — gateway 504s drop to <1% in last 3m. :thumbsup:
lee (support): Noted customer confirms fewer errors now. They're running another burst test.
emily (ml-op): For long term: model init time is 100–120s. We should add a warmup hook that loads model weights in background during scale event, and pre-warm a small pool for flagged customers. Also consider lowering KEDA pollingInterval to 10s for critical queues.
anika (customer-success): I'll coordinate with the customer about billing — we should avoid auto-suspension during stress tests. @billing-bot / billing team: can you whitelist stress tests or at least change action to 429 not revoke token for these accounts?
billing-bot: Created ticket BILL-8943 to review automated suspension rules for high-volume test accounts. Assigned to billing ops.
jonathan (sre): Follow-ups/todo list:
- infra: reduce KEDA polling to 10s for the model-pool OR add prometheus alert on queue growth (rahul)
- ml-op: implement warmup hook & document model init time per model (emily)
- devex/support: add guidance to support runbook about requiring minReplicaCount=1 for customer stress tests (lee/anika)
- billing: review auto-suspend/emergency whitelist (billing ops)
Set owners and expected ETA: rahul 2h for KEDA tweak and emergency config; emily 1 week for warmup; lee/anika 24h to update runbook; billing TBD.

maria (oncall): Also add an infra alert to detect when readiness probe failures spike during scale events — we had probe failures correlate with 502s.
jonathan (sre): I posted a short log snippet from the gateway showing the timeline:
```
10:40:12 GET /v1/generate rid=abc123 -> 403 token_revoked
10:40:20 spike -> queue length 420
10:40:45 KEDA triggers scale -> new pods scheduled
10:41:50 pod model-abc-0 init: loading weights (took 115s)
10:42:10 kube endpoint update -> pod ready
10:42:15 gateway -> 200s returned
```
lee (support): Customer sent repro steps — they used loadtest tool with 500 concurrent requests for 30s. We'll include that in the ticket.
anika (customer-success): Customer is satisfied with mitigation. They'll wait for permanent fix and billing review before resuming heavy tests. I'll keep them updated.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback completed for model-pool image tag v2.3.1 -> v2.3.0 as requested by @rahul
maria (oncall): Good catch everyone. We'll track this in INCIDENT-2026-11-01-autoscale-coldstart. Assigning postmortem. Closing thread for active coordination, keep posting updates here if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
